title: Arecanut — Irrigation Management and Dry Season Water Schedule
content:
ARECANUT IRRIGATION:

CRITICAL PERIOD:
November to May (dry season) — without irrigation, severe yield loss and palm death possible.

WATER REQUIREMENT:
- 200 L/palm/week during peak dry season (January-April).
- 150 L/palm/week in November-December.
- No irrigation needed during southwest monsoon (June-September).

IRRIGATION METHODS:
1. DRIP IRRIGATION (Recommended):
- 16-20 LPH emitters at 60 cm from palm base.
- 2 drippers/palm.
- Irrigate 2-3 hours daily in dry season.
- Saves 60% water compared to flood irrigation.

2. BASIN IRRIGATION:
- Basin diameter: 2-3 m around palm.
- Apply 200 L/palm/week.
- Mulch basin with dry coconut fronds, paddy straw to conserve moisture.

3. SPRINKLER:
- Rotating sprinkler @ 4 m radius.
- Suitable for large gardens on flat terrain.

MULCHING (Important):
- Apply green/dry leaves 10-15 cm thick in basins.
- Reduces evaporation, maintains soil moisture.
- Use fallen arecanut fronds, paddy straw.

STRESS INDICATORS:
- Yellowing and browning of older fronds — first sign of moisture stress.
- Rapid nut fall — severe stress indicator.
- If stress occurs: Emergency irrigation + KNO3 0.5% foliar spray.

KARNATAKA (Shivamogga/Sagara/Sirsi region):
- Area has good rainfall (2500-3500 mm/year) — irrigation needed only Dec-May.
- Gravity-fed drip from hillside tanks — traditional practice in Malnad region.
